 Order
Heard finally with the consent of the parties at motion stage.

1. This appeal by the appellants/claimants u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 08.01.2019 passed by First Additional MACT, District-Dhar in Claim Case No.24/18 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and findings recorded by the claims tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3.

As per findings of the tribunal, in the case of death of Prakash, amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.11,41,000/- has been awarded by the tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till realization.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that compensation as awarded by the tribunal by accepting earning Rs.5000/- per month is inadequate looking to the age of the deceased as he was working as Raaj Mistri (skilled labourer).

Hence, it is prayed that accepting earning of the deceased as Rs.7,125/- p.m. keeping in view the circular of Madhya Pradesh Government in respect of wages for labourers, applying adequate --3-- multiplier and adding future prospects, reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company contended that claims tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and supported the findings recorded by the claims tribunal.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court, just and proper income of the deceased would be Rs.7,125/- per month according to circular of Labour Department, Madhya Pradesh Government for laborers.
7. Learned counsel for the appellants has further submits that tribunal has committed error in not granting consortium in each and every head.

sentences.text: (Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020) arising out of SLP (Civil) No.28548/2014 has held that wife, parents and children are also entitled to get consortium so tribunal has committed error in granting only Rs.40,000/- in the head of consortium, hence, in this head, amount must be increased from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.2,00,000/-.
9. In view of the aforesaid discussion, in the opinion of this Court, compensation amount deserves to be enhanced.

Hence, the break-up of enhancement in the compensation amount is as under:-
Annual Income : Rs.7,125+2850 (40% future prospects) =9975X12=Rs.88,350/- per annum After deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses (88,350/4 = 22,087.5) and applying subtraction (88350-22087.5)
, total income comes to Rs.66,262.5 per annum.
After applying multiplier of 17, total income comes to Rs.11,26,462.5 (Rs.66,262.5X17)

Therefore, calculation of the amount will be as under:-
--4--  Total income : Rs.11,26,462.5  For consortium : Rs.2,40,000/-

Funeral Expenses : Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of Estate : Rs.15,000/-

Total amount : Rs.13,96,462.5/-
10.
Keeping in view the aforesaid, present appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.
The amount of compensation is enhanced from Rs.11,41,000/- to Rs.13,96,462.5/- with interest as fixed by the tribunal over and above the amount already awarded by the tribunal.
Hence, the total amount enhanced in this appeal is Rs.2,55,462.5 (Rs.13,96,462.5-11,41,000/-).

Accordingly,
the appellants shall be entitled to receive the enhanced amount of Rs.2,55,462.5 over and and above the amount which has already been awarded by the tribunal.
All other findings recorded by the tribunal shall remain intact.
The present appeal stands disposed of.
